title: a plain projection of a durable input reaches the Plan as an explicit input expression carrying its path
notes: specification/durable-execution.mdx:63 (Flow): 'Property access and argument passing on a symbolic result MUST create typed projections and dependency edges when representable in Plan IR', read together with :59 'It MUST NOT invoke the source function with proxy or symbolic JavaScript values to discover the graph.' This is the paired positive control for the thirteen refusal cases added to this area on 2026-08-26: every one of them is THIS program with one operator inserted, so without this case the refusals could be about the shared boilerplate (a `return Action.run(...)` with no postfix `!`, an Action whose input field is not the flow's own input type) rather than about the operator, and the whole set would be pinning the wrong thing. It is also the only case in the corpus that opens a Plan value expression. The five observed lines say, in order: the descriptor marker; the lowered node kinds; that the Action argument became an `object` expression; that its `v` field became an `input` expression rather than a folded `literal`; and that the projection kept its path. The fourth line is the anti-folding observation and it is the reason the case exists in this shape: a lowering that discovered the graph by evaluating the source function against a stand-in object would emit a `literal` here, and nothing else in the corpus would notice. Every narrowing failure prints a distinct sentence instead of an empty line, so no branch of this program can satisfy the expectation by observing nothing. HONEST NOTE ON HOW THIS CASE WAS WRITTEN: the first draft printed `JSON.stringify(node.input)` and declared `{"kind":"object","fields":{"v":{"kind":"input","path":["mode"]}}}`. Both backends print the same object with its keys canonicalized (`{"fields":...,"kind":...}`), so the draft was red on a key order the specification does not name and this case does not promise. The CASE was rewritten to observe the promise directly rather than the serialization -- the expectation was not re-baselined onto a stringified form, because pinning a JSON key order here would have quietly made this case a second, unannounced ratification of the unsettled comptime/canonical ordering question recorded in COVERAGE.md. Verified load-bearing rather than assumed: mutating the fourth stdout line from `input` to `literal` turns the case red on both backends with the stdout diff printed, and the file was restored byte-identically (sha256 compared before and after). SOURCE NARROWED 2026-08-28, expectation unchanged. `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` became enforced (compatibility.mdx §Mandatory, previously unimplemented), and this program read an index without narrowing, so it was correctly refused. §Mandatory's own guidance is that such a read 'MUST be narrowed, or read through an extraction helper'. The narrowing is inert at run time — the guard never fires — so the stdout this case pins is byte-for-byte what it was, re-derived by running both backends.
